newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends down 50 cts as Nov delivery weigh.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends down 50 cts as Nov delivery weigh.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended down 50 cents a tonne at $219.75 on December after some weakness on heating oil in the United States which resumed trading after the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.
"There been no significant change. $216.50 is good support, thats the important number," said Alastair Harris of brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.
Jan ended 25 cents lower at $216.25 but Feb was up 25 cents.
Earlier, Dec gas oil also softened on news that more than 160,000 tonnes bought through the November IPE contract would be sold into ARA, brokers said.
Dec gas oil fell to $218.50, the day's low, on expected oversupply in the key Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp market.

AIC said on Monday that Cargill had failed to lift 160,000-190,000 tonnes it bought through the IPE and said it would sell in the ARA barge market. Cargill said it was working with the IPE on issues relating to the November delivery prodecure.

Meanwhile, Brent edged higher in the afternoon despite the impending return of Iraq to the market. Iraqi Foreign Minister Saeed al-Sahaf was quoted in Iraqi newspapers as saying that Iraq had started striking deals with foreign firms for the sale of oil under its oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
The broker said Iraq's return to the market could push prices lower in the short-term if it coincided with bigger loading programmes from the North Sea.
Jan Brent was up 10 cents at $22.87 at 1745 GMT just two cents below the day's high.
